The system shall help the user avoid making mistakes while scheduling classes and clinicals for the nursing students.
2 out of 3 Program Administrators/Nursing Staff Members shall successfully be able to use the system to manage the scheduling of classes and clinicals.
The system shall be expected to manage the nursing program curriculum and class/clinical scheduling for a minimum of 5 years.
The system shall have basic data integrity checking to reduce the possibility of incorrect or invalid data being introduced.
The system shall protect private information in accordance with the organization’s information policy.
A cohort shall be associated to one Program of Study offered by the department.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add a listing of students to a cohort.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add a single student to a cohort
Students added to a cohort shall be eligible for the cohort’s Program of Study.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to specify the preferred sequence of classes for a given cohort.
For each class within a sequence for a cohort Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to specify which quarter that class will be offered.
For each class within a sequence for a cohort Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to specify which quarter that class will be offered.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add new classes to a sequence of classes
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add clinical classes or sections to a sequence of classes
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add a new cohort to the system identified by start month and year.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add new classes for the nursing department into the system.
A class shall be either a non-clinical class or a clinical class.
A non-clinical class shall specify the course name lecture room requirements and instructor needs.
A clinical class shall specify the course name lecture room requirements clinical site needs lecture instructor needs and clinical lab instructor needs.
Program Administrators/Nursing Staff Members shall be able to create a new Program of Study.
A Program of Study shall consist of a program name and listing of required classes (both clinical and non-clinical) that must be completed.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall have the ability to specify which classes are required for a Program of Study
The system shall be able to display a report of needed classes for a given quarter for all cohorts of all programs for Program Administrators/Nursing Staff Members’ planning purposes.
The report of needed classes shall include (but not be limited to) classes to be offered number of sections needed number of labs needed and room types needed.
Classes for a given cohort shall not conflict with regards to the time and day that they are offered.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add a new clinical site into the system.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add a new clinical lab section for an existing clinical class into the System.
A clinical lab section shall include the clinical site name the class instructor day and time of the lab.
Program Administrators and Nursing Staff Members shall be able to add a student who has registered for a clinical class to a clinical lab section for that class.
Program Administrators/Nursing Staff Members shall be able to cancel a clinical lab section only if there are no students registered for that clinical lab section.
A Program Administrator/Nursing Staff Member shall be able to add a new nursing student to the system.

The system shall be able to display a printable summary for individual clinical labs which will include (but not be limited to) class name class number lab section listing of students enrolled instructor day(s) time and location.
The system shall be able to display a printable summary of the system log.

The system shall contain contact information (e-mail and phone number) for all people relevant to the system including (but not limited to) staff members students lecture instructors clinical lab instructors and clinical site administrators.
The system will use the stored e-mail addresses as a primary means of communicating information to affected parties.

The system will notify affected parties for routine communication purposes including but not limited to informing students of upcoming offered classes (timeline) and what their schedule will be/shall be.

Program Administrators/Nursing Staff Members shall have the ability to modify information relating to cohorts including cohort identifier program of study preferred sequence of classes and quarters that a cohort will be taking specific classes.

Program Administrators/Nursing Staff Members shall have the ability to modify information relating to a Program of Study within the Nursing Department including the Program of study name and required classes for that Program of Study.

Program Administrators/Nursing Staff Members shall have the ability to modify information relating to a Nursing Student including student ID student name phone number e-mail status (full time or part time) and program of study.
The list of dispute cases that are displayed after a search is performed must be color coded for easy identification of dispute cases based upon the dispute case status.
Only users with Update access must be able to initiate dispute requests.
All additions of new users and modifications to user’s access shall be recorded on the User Report.
If a user account is revoked it can only be re-instantiated by the System Administrator.
Only the System Administrator shall be able to reset a revoked user logon account
The Disputes application shall manipulate and view business data. Users will not have direct access to data files or databases.
All updates to data files or database must be initiated from the Disputes System.
All actions that modify an existing dispute case must be recorded in the case history.
The Disputes System shall provide update access capability for authorized users of the application.

The Disputes System must allow the users to select disputable transactions (based on the age of the transaction) from a user interface and initiate a dispute (ticket retrieval request or chargeback notification) on the selected transaction.
The Disputes System must provide the user the ability to initiate a single dispute case on multiple transactions that belong to a single merchant.

The Disputes System must allow the user to create three unique types of ticket retrieval requests. The three types of ticket retrieval requests are (1) Request for original receipt (2) Request for a copy of the receipt or (3) Request for a portfolio. A portfolio consists of documentation that would provide proof of a purchase such as the documentation that is received from a car rental agency that is more than a sales receipt.
The Disputes System must prevent external users from requesting original receipts. Requests for original receipts are restricted to internal users.

The Disputes System must provide a confirmation to the user upon the creation of ticket retrieval request that contains the following information the dispute case number the type of retrieval requested (copy original or portfolio) and the date that the merchant response is due.

The Disputes System must provide a confirmation to the user upon the creation of a chargeback request. The confirmation must contain the following information the dispute case number the type of chargeback requested (pending or immediate) and the date that the merchant response is due.
The Disputes System shall prevent the creation of duplicate dispute requests 100% of the time.

The Disputes System shall accurately provide a list of possible reason codes for a given transaction. The list of possible reason codes must be derived based on the type of transaction and the industry that the merchant belongs to according to the business rules defined for the Disputes System.
The Disputes System must provide the ability to view existing dispute cases.

A list of all disputes cases that meet the entered search criteria must be provided to the user. The list of cases must differentiate the type and/or status of the case by color -coding the line item in the list. For example all open cases will be yellow and all closed cases will be gray.
The Disputes System shall provide the users the ability to view the history of all activities that have occurred on the dispute case.

The Dispute System shall provide the users with the ability to follow up on a dispute case via follow-up actions. The list of available follow up actions for a given dispute case must be filtered by the status of the case and the access level of the user.

For any systematic (non-user initiated) action that occurs on a case such as the disputes aging process a case activity will be generated. Upon the next logon the user that initiated the dispute case must be notified that a systematic action has occurred on the dispute case.
All letter requests must be formatted according to guidelines specified by the Print Letter Utility system.
Any disputes cases that have been closed for over 6 months must be purged from the online disputes database.
The search for recycled parts shall take no longer than 15 seconds. The search results shall be returned in under 15 seconds.
The recycled parts audit report shall be returned to the user within 10 seconds. The audit report shall be returned within 10 seconds.
The preferred repair facility ratings shall be saved within 5 seconds. The save shall occur within 5 seconds.
Only adjusters can request recycled parts audit reports. No users without an adjuster role shall request recycled parts audits.
Only adjusters with a supervisor role can update preferred repair facility ratings. Users without the supervisor role cannot access the repair facility ratings.
Only collision estimators shall search for recycled parts. Users without the collision estimator role shall not have access to the search for recycled parts.
One insurance company shall not be able to view another insurance companys claim data.
The system shall prevent malicious attacks including denial of service.
The user shall search for the preferred repair facility using vehicle vehicle location and radius in miles
The vehicle data shall include vehicle year make and model
The vehicle location shall include street address city state and zipcode
The system shall resolve the zipcode for the street address city and state if zipcode is unknown.
The search radius shall be between 1 and 30 miles
The system shall locate the preferred repair facility with the highest ratings for the input criteria
The adjuster shall enter the preferred repair facility on the estimate assignment.
The adjuster shall be able to override the preferred repair facitlity on the estimate assignment.
The preferred repair facility shall be returned to the user.
The estimator shall search for available recycled parts using damaged vehicle parts information.
The estimator shall search for available recycled parts using a list of preferred parts suppliers.
The system shall search for available recycled parts for the supplied vehicle parts and suppliers.
The estimator shall search by zipcode with a radius of 30 miles if no parts are found for the preferred parts suppliers
The system shall retain the available recycled parts and suppliers returned from the search.
The available recycled parts information and their suppliers shall be returned to the user.
The estimator shall apply selected recycled parts to the collision estimate.
The estimator shall not apply recycled parts to the collision estimate if no available parts are returned.
The adjuster shall request a recycled parts audit of the collision estimate.
The recycled parts search results provided to the estimator shall be retrieved by the system.
The audit report shall include the total number of recycled parts used in the estimate.
The audit report shall include the percentage of available recycled parts used in the estimate
The audit report shall include the total score of the audit which sums the indivual line items.
The audit report shall be displayed to the user.
The audit report shall be available to other adjusters at later points in time.
The current repair facility ratings shall be displayed to the user.
The system will display a blank set of ratings if there are not ratings yet defined.
The ratings shall be from a scale of 1-10
The ratings shall include categories for attempted use of recycled parts and actual use of recycled parts
The user shall select to save the preferred repair facility ratings.
The preferred repair facility ratings shall be saved by the system.

The product shall record updated meeting agendas.
The product shall send a meeting confirmation to the meeting organizer.

The product shall display conference rooms according to search parameters.

The product shall notify building personnel of equipment transport requests.

The System shall not require additional third party licenses resulting in royalty fees.

All streaming movie sales will be logged in the database and accessible by the administrator.

Daily usage statistics should be logged and accessible by the administrator.

The product shall display the grids within a circle as a view from a periscope.
The product shall display each type of ship in a grid using an image of the specific type of ship.
When the offensive player takes a shot the product shall simulate the sound of a ship at sea.
When a shot is marked as a miss the product shall simulate the sound of a shot missing its target.
When a shot is marked as a hit the product shall simulate the sound of a shot hitting its target.
When a ship is sunk the product shall simulate the sound of a sinking ship.
The product shall provide players no access to information that might reveal the identity of another player
The product shall maintain a list of players.
The product shall make inactive players unavailable for selection from the list of players.
The product shall remove players who have been inactive for 24 hours from the list of players.
The product shall prevent a player from viewing the offensive or defensive grids of the other player.
The product shall prevent the player from overlapping ships on their grid.
When both players have positioned their 5 ships on their defensive grids the product shall define the status of each player for the first turn.
For each turn the product shall identify one player as offensive status and one player as defensive status.
The product shall maintain the status of each player for a turn either offensive or defensive.
At the start of each turn the product shall notify each player of his or her status.
For each shot the product shall examine the defensive grid of the defensive player to determine whether the shot was a hit or miss.
For each shot the product shall mark the shot as a hit or miss on the defensive grid of the defensive player.
For each shot the product shall mark the shot as a hit or miss on the offensive grid of the offensive player.
When the hit results in sinking a ship the product shall notify the players that the ship was sunk.
When the hit results in sinking a ship the product shall mark the ship as sunk on the defensive grid of the defensive player.
When the hit results in sinking a ship the product shall indicate the type of ship sunk on the defensive grid of the defensive player.
When the hit results in sinking a ship the product shall mark the ship as sunk on the offensive grid of the offensive player.
If the shot was marked as a miss the product shall change the status of the offensive player to defensive
If the shot was marked as a miss the product shall change the status of the defensive player to offensive
The product shall continue to assign turns until the game is ended.
The product shall end a game when a hit by the offensive player results in sinking the last of the defensive player’s ships which had not been previously marked as sunk.
The product shall allow a player to end a game at any time during the game.
When a game is ended the product shall notify the players that the game is ended.

All CCR users shall receive training before the WCS system is deployed. One training session will be held for 100% of CCR users before system deployment (based on a CCR user being available)
The WCS system shall have the ability to connect other designated WCS databases currently not included in the system.
The WCS system shall have the ability to include data for regions outside the United States and be accessed by users outside of the United States if approved by CCR management.

The Brio portion of the WCS system must be able to export files in spreadsheet form (Microsoft Excel and Lotus 1-2-3 formats). Brio will provide buttons in the user interface that produce/export reports in .xls or .123 file formats.

The GCS shall transmit the UAV's properties to the GCSMiddleware
The GCS shall transmit the UAV's current location to the GCSMiddleware
The GCSMiddleware shall handle state messages monitoring messages and mode change messages received from an GCS.
The GCSMiddleware shall follow a predefined set of steps to establish a connection between a GCS and Dronology
The GCSMiddleware shall handle multiple GCS
Each route shall include a unique ID a textual description and a set of waypoints all of which are editable in the UI.
The RouteCreationUI shall only accept valid altitude and speed values for waypoint.
The RouteCreationUI shall distinguish between starting ending and intermediate waypoint markers.
A user may reorder routes or remove flight plans assigned to a UAV as long as the flight has not started execution.
The RouteAssignmentUI shall provide means to select an existing routes and assign them to a UAV.
When loading the map view it shall be positioned at the pre-defined location
The UIMiddleware shall accept and activate a mission plan upon request.
The UIMiddleware shall enable an existing route to be assigned to an active UAV.
The UIMiddleware shall enable the creation and modification of flight routes
The UIMiddleware shall provide a list of all active UAVs
The InternalSimulator shall approximate the state of the battery
When given a landing command the InternalSimulator shall move the UAV from to the ground altitude corresponding to its current longitude and latitude.

When given a goto command the InternalSimulator shall update the location of the UAV at increments of {{SIMULATIONSTEPSIZE}} meters moving it towards the target destination until the destination is reached.
When given a takeoff command the InternalSimulator shall move the UAV to the takeoff altitude corresponding to its current longitude and latitude.
The UAVRegistrationManager shall store UAV meta-data information such as the UAV's technical characteristics
When the maximum numbers of allowed activated UAVs has been reached the UAVActivationManager shall reject any further activation requests.
When a UAV is deactivated the UAVActivationManager shall cancel all current and scheduled flight plans
The VehicleCore shall support virtual UAVs
The VehicleCore shall support UAVs connected via the GCS
If requested the SingleUAVFlightPlanScheduler shall abort the currently executing flight plan of an UAV
When requested if a mission is currently active the MissionPlanner shall cancel the active mission.
The MissionPlanner shall manage predefined FlightPatterns
If a flight route is assigned to a UAV which is currently hovering in place the FlightManager shall assign the route and maintain the hover in place mode.
When the hover in place command is issued the FlightManager shall halt the UAV in place and maintain its current position.
When given two coordinates the CoordinateSystem shall compute the distance between them.
When a flight route requires a customized takeoff altitude that differs from the system's default takeoff altitude it shall be specified in the flight route.
The FlightRouteManager shall persist flight routes.
The FlightRouteManager shall ensure that all flight routes represent a {{VALIDFLIGHTROUTE}}.
When the GCS loses the connection to an UAV the GCS shall attempt to reconnect
When a GCS requests activation of a newly detected UAV the GCSMiddleware shall forward the request to Dronology.
The ObjectAvoidance system only issues commands within the capabilities of the UAV
When a stationary or moving object is within the proximity of a UAV the ObjectAvoidance system shall issue evasive directives to the UAV
When the RealTimeFlightUI is loaded a map shall be displayed.
The UIMiddleware shall only assign one control-client at a time for each UAV.
When a UAV's current flight is cancelled the SingleUAVFlightPlanScheduler shall in turn cancel all scheduled flight plans for that UAV.
If a UAV has pending flight plans then when it reaches the final waypoint of its current flight plan the SingleUAVFlightPlanScheduler shall execute the next assigned flight plan.
Each waypoint shall be specified using coordinates that include longitude latitude and altitude.
The VehicleCore shall associate a {{UAVTYPE}} for each UAV defining its basic attributes.
The UAVActivationManager shall ensure that only one instance of each registered drone is active at any time.
The SingleUAVFlightPlanScheduler shall only execute one flight plan at a time for each UAV.
The VehicleCore shall assign a unique ID to each activated UAV.
When requested the VehicleCore shall shall transition the UAV between states according to allowed state transitions as depicted in the UAV state transition diagram
The system must offer customisable workflow to import or create metadata and upload associated files and support multiple ingest protocols e.g. SWORD2
The system must ingest and store metadata at a data object level, where a data object is a folder that contains one or more files
The system must support multiple files types including multimedia.
The system must support controlled lists against some metadata fields, either held locally or drawn from an external source e.g. Subject vocabularies
The system should support customisation of out of the box help text and provide context sensitive feedback for the depositor e.g. Highlight missing metadata fields, file upload failure alert.
The system must support staged deposit workflow including an administrative area for quality checking prior to data publication.
The system must enable selective harvesting of metadata, including support for OAI-PMH sets; offer API functionality to re-users, conforming to open standards.
The system must enable extraction of metadata and data in an open format e.g. to enable migration to another repository platform.
The system should support different types of relationship within and between data sets e.g. IsVersionOf; Is Part Of; References etc. and support navigation between related datasets.
The system should support additional depositor generated and re-user generated metadata.
The system should auto-generate preservation metadata.
The system must support versioning of datasets including clear indication of the latest version.
The system should display file size, format and software application and version for re-users
The system must support technical metadata related to specific files or datasets.
The system must support generation of persistent unique identifiers for datasets including DOIs.
The system could visualise and process data within the repository system.
The system should unpack a range of file archive formats (e.g. Zip, tar, gz, bz) to allow navigation through the archive folder structure and selective download
The system could support optional end user alerts e.g.to be notified of data change or new versions.
The system must enable depositor and repository manager to specify granular access rights to the deposited data files at collection and data object level.
The system should enable depositor and repository manager to specify granular access rights to the deposited data files at individual file level.
The system must support embargo options for metadata and/or associated files at collection, data object and file level.
The system must enable immediate access to and download of datasets where available
The system must support permanent data destruction to meet any legal or ethical requirements.
The system must manage granular access to data and its associated metadata, including data held securely in a dark archive.

The system must generate a variety of reports analysing repository content, including records associated with an academic unit, a funder, grant number, data creator and analysis of data by format, file size and embargo and access conditions.
The system must hold funder and grant metadata associated with one or more repository records.
The system should support reporting by funder to confirm a particular funder's open access data / deposit requirement has been met.
The system should generate reports on repository content growth pattern over time.
The system should support preservation function by generating reports on repository content.
The system should generate reports on the number and origins of repository end users, including by domain type and geographical location.

The system must report on number and speed of data downloads and log number of data requests. Reports should be possible over specified periods of time and against specified subsets of the repository (by Funder, by Creator, by academic unit).
The system must allow specification of mandatory metadata fields.
The system should retain history of changes to metadata fields
The system must possess a field for multiple data owners over time (previous owners should not be overwritten).
The system must import or harvest metadata and associated files from a variety of sources using established standards such as OAI-PMH, OAI-ORE.
The system must harvest / ingest / import metadata from other systems e.g. funder, grant number, equipment, author identifier, project code.
The system should be able to support externally managed unique entities e.g. identifiers such as ORCID, ResearcherID
The system could display linked data from other systems using open standards.
The system must link to associated research outputs, potentially in other systems e.g. Published papers.
The system could supply data to research management systems (for example, to enable reporting against the percentage of projects with data associated, analysable by Funder and academic unit).
The system could import and display impact measures such as citation data from external sources e.g. Thomson Reuters Data Citation Index and track alt-metrics such as links and likes.
